body:
My suggestion would be to change the function prototype as follows:

```cpp
void godot_init_profiler(int argc, char **argv);
```

In the implementation of the function the selected profiling system should only be enabled, if a "--enable-profiler" or similar command line parameter is passed to Godot. This way (at least in the case of Perfetto) production builds of the engine can be delivered to end users, because when profiling is not enabled, the performance impact is negligible.

Note, that I don't propose to include Perfetto or Tracy in the official builds, only if someone is building a custom release build of the engine, they can easily include profiling functionality.

+		// When perfetto is updated, the internals may change, and this code may have to be revisited.
+		::perfetto::internal::ValidateEventNameType<decltype(nullptr)>();
+		namespace tns = PERFETTO_TRACK_EVENT_NAMESPACE;
+		if (is_dynamic_category) {
+			tns::TrackEvent::CallIfEnabled([&](uint32_t instances) PERFETTO_NO_THREAD_SAFETY_ANALYSIS {

+						::perfetto::internal::DecayEventNameType(nullptr),
+						::perfetto::protos::pbzero::TrackEvent::TYPE_SLICE_END);
+			});
+		} else {
+			tns::TrackEvent::CallIfCategoryEnabled(this->category_idx,

+								::perfetto::internal::DecayEventNameType(nullptr),

+		_end_now();
+	}

It looks like the same approach with the TRACY_ENABLE implementation. Was the destructor for tracy designed to be idempotent?

Edit: Ah I see, tracy macros use placement new to instead, so the same approach could work for the perfetto macros.

With the perfetto macros, this is going to end this group step at the end of the if statement scope, which looks like a mistake in the resulting trace (there will be a gap in the trace which seems to defeat the purpose of the Grouped API). You probably want a regular event here:

GodotProfileZone("movie_writer->add_frame");

With the tracy macros, this kinda works because of the placement new taking over the existing object's scope, but it's also kind of an anti-pattern for a trace macro's scope to continue beyond the code scope -- ie this "add_frame" event will actually include a bunch of code after this if statement's scope ends, so that could cause some confusion when trying to reason about the cost of this codepath. "add_frame" might look really expensive even though it was actually some slow code on lines 4860-4881.

Maybe a good rule for this GodotProfileZoneGrouped API is to only use it in a single scope? And for any child scopes just use an additional GodotProfileZone().
Use GodotProfileZone instead for this sub scope?

It gets complicated quickly, but it is super powerful in perfetto to see some data on events sometimes.

I added this support to the perfetto C API wrapper project (percetto): https://github.com/olvaffe/percetto/blob/main/src/percetto.h#L658

General design comment: it's nice if you can easily find the code that corresponds to the trace event name. I find it nice to trace whole functions with names like "Class::method" to satisfy that goal, and then use simpler names like this "_end_frame" when it's already within a traced function scope.

Yea, generally I've been preferring the `Class::function` when it's meaningful, but in some cases it wasn't, especially when the zone was just part of some arbitrary group. It would be nice to find a pattern to use, but currently it's just the "Ivorius has been doing his best" pattern 😅
It's not supposed to be a sub scope in this case, it should replace the previous grouped scope.
Yea, I'm hoping we can expand the API to add support for indices in both tracy and perfetto in a future PR>

I was thinking it is unexpected that this _sort_active_viewports scope continues beyond the end of this if statement (similar to my comment above). Since it's called "_sort_active_viewports" I guess it should only trace this call to _sort_active_viewports(), and GodotProfileZone does exactly that (at least, that's how things would work with the perfetto UI -- this GodotProfileZone would be stacked underneath the parent  "prepare viewports" event).

Stacking `_sort_active_viewports` below `prepare viewports` would be possible, if this statement used `GodotProfileZone` instead, as you suggested.
However, in this case this is not wanted, because `prepare viewports` doesn't (in my mind) include sorting the viewports. It's a different step.
Ending the `_sort_active_viewports` might be nice, but I'd prefer to investigate that in a follow-up PR. It would require adding a _new_ object on every `GodotProfileZoneGrouped` call, and ending the grouped scope when it is destructed, which might result in a lot of added complexity.

Yea, I see the problem. I think the correct solution would be to re-write the perfetto macros to work like the tracy ones.
I can probably do this with a Godot helper, but I'd need to dive into the APIs more. And as mentioned earlier, I currently can't run perfetto, because it's refusing to cooperate with me.

As much as I'd love to solve this, I think I'd prefer to merge the PR, so we can get to work correcting the implementations later. The important part of this PR is the API design; the implementation can always be improved later.
